tasks.title: Notify proves contract parity and ledger compatibility before api updates
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, R7, all Precondition checks, parity test, mixed check M3, existing-test controls and Completion evidence; Evidence R2/R3 table, Rollout order step 2 and rollback, Security impact, Performance impact and Acceptance evidence 4-8. Includes the revised writer-first rollback sequence and both database/ledger verification checks.

acceptance.expected: Before any edit, state is CLOSED. If OPEN, request a needs-input hold naming #820; preserve fan-out coordination for a person to link this child as blocked by #820.
Before any edit read main's contract pin as PIN; PATCH_SHA is the merged contract child's patch commit.
First status is ahead or identical, second ahead. Request needs-input if the pin is older/incompatible, or a hold if the patch is already present (identical or behind on the second comparison).

For every row of Evidence's R2/R3 table, compare notify's channelSchema('email') safeParse success and contract validateNotifyChannelDefinition ok, and assert both equal that row's independent literal notify-0464b90 boolean. Address rows run separately for from and to[0]. Include literal clientName '☃' (U+2603) with false, plus 'münchen.test' and '☃.example.test' false; real NUL, underscore, malformed-label/literal rows and hostname/address-literal positives all follow the table. Exclude 201..255-character names; contract retains its 200 cap. On the old prepatch pin exactly bold defect rows fail by assertion on contract's result; controls pass. On the patch all tests pass, 0 fail, irrespective of focused-run coverage exit; record both results.

M3: the specified padded-address email record in a valid revision envelope gives kind:'applied', exactly one record, original from 'Ops < ops@example.test >' and rejected:[]. A temp ledger accepts replaceRemoteChannels with id:'mail', appliedAt:1, revision 'sha256-' + 64 literal '1' digits, and the literal canonical JSON D in the notify section; after close/reopen remoteChannels returns that unchanged row and definition text. Both fail by assertion with the old pin (element rejected and LedgerRowError) and pass with the patch; no fixture/install crashes count as red evidence.

Both files pin the same full 40-character SHA of the merged pulse-contract main commit containing R1-R6, independently identified from the contract child's merged PR; preserve intervening merged features.
All tests pass, 0 fail (focused coverage is not the full gate). Existing remote-channel SMTP rejection and ledger tests keep passing; no notify-local schema/mailer rule or message changes.
exit 0; frozen install, lint, typecheck and the full test suite pass with the repository's existing coverage threshold; no tooling, coverage or budget gate is weakened.

Run five times per side, alternating origin/main and candidate with their installed pins, and report each side's median of user + system CPU seconds in the PR; wall time is not CPU. Expected about +0.1 s test CPU. Report an increase above 0.5 s as a finding.

acceptance.command: bun -e 'const t=process.cpuUsage(); await import("@lorenzh/pulse-contract"); const c=process.cpuUsage(t); Bun.gc(true); console.log((c.user+c.system)/1000, process.memoryUsage().rss/1048576)'
acceptance.expected: After installing each side's pin, take 15 alternating fresh-process samples per side (origin/main and candidate); report median import CPU ms and RSS MiB in the PR. Account for eager subscription module imports from 2.5.0; report an increase above 10 ms or 2 MiB as a finding. Expected near zero pin-import delta after prerequisite #820 has moved notify to 2.5.0; otherwise about +1.4 ms CPU and +0.1 MiB.

acceptance.command: bun bench/run.ts --a <api main SHA> --b <api main SHA> --others-ref main --b-ref notify=<notify branch SHA> --service-tokens --expect-report notify --rounds 3
acceptance.expected: From the api bench checkout, with literal resolved SHAs substituted, run full A/B when Docker/Compose is available and report results without budget regressions (api bench/README.md:76-100). Otherwise state the concrete Docker limitation and that the nightly main bench is the gating check after merge. Expect no measurable load/latency change and only the startup/memory effects of Performance impact.

acceptance.command: git diff origin/main --stat -- src && git diff --check && gh pr view --json body,statusCheckRollup
acceptance.expected: No src diff; whitespace check and required CI check pass. PR records #820/pin preconditions, parity defect/control results including '☃':false, M3 old/new results, full patch SHA, test CPU/startup A/B and full-bench-or-nightly evidence. Security checklist confirms secret-safe errors, nonthrowing validation and full frozen pin. Merge/activate notify before api; carry the first-deploy api/console/notify patch requirement and the complete writer-first rollback sequence in the next check. Old notify rejects M3's padded definition D and exits 2 when reopening a ledger that holds it.

PR carries the exact 'Releases, deploy and rollback' rule: api leaves the patch first on every running instance, even for a console-only or notify-only rollback. Its old pin rejects newly accepted addresses such as 'Ops < ops@example.test >' on POST/PUT with 422 (M1), while patched readers still read existing rows. Keep writes of that set stopped throughout cleanup and reader rollback, until both readers run the patch again; if api cannot leave the patch, retain patched console/notify. Only after api is reverted everywhere, normalize every padded from/to entry through PUT /admin/notify/channels/<id> using the current revision in If-Match; delete shadowed rows through DELETE instead (PUT answers 409). Never edit database/ledger rows by hand. Require contract c5ce6685ce8b563a243823bca451032291b81adb's validateAdminNotifyChannelsView on GET /admin/notify/channels to give ok:true. Require service.report.appliedRevision equal to revision and service.report.rejected equal to []; a matching revision alone cannot prove cleanup because rejected ids retain their earlier ledger rows. Then stop notify, read SELECT id, definition FROM remote_channels from PULSE_NOTIFY_STATE, and require the same old contract's validateNotifyChannelDefinition to give ok:true on every parsed definition. Only after both database and stopped-ledger checks pass may console and notify roll back, in either order. If either cannot be proved, keep patched readers. Api returns to the patch only after both readers run it again. This is rollout/rollback guidance in the PR, not an instruction to roll back a live service during implementation.
